l4_steps.name: Receive AOG defect notification
l4_steps.input: Pilot-raised defect entry via ETL or ACARS message from flight deck
l4_steps.output: AOG defect record opened in MRO system with timestamp and station
l4_steps.pain_point: ETL systems at outstations may lack real-time ACARS integration, forcing phone-based defect relay that delays MCC awareness by 10–20 min

l4_steps.name: Assess defect against MEL / CDL
l4_steps.input: Defect description, aircraft type/registration, departure time
l4_steps.output: MEL/CDL applicability decision: relief granted or AOG confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: MEL assessment completed < 15 minutes of defect receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL revision cycles lag OEM amendments by up to 30 days if airline OpSpec approval is delayed, leaving engineers working from printed fallback copies

l4_steps.name: Apply MEL relief and replan dispatch
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + Amadeus Altéa Operations
l4_steps.input: MEL relief decision, any associated placard or operational restriction
l4_steps.output: MEL deferred defect item raised, aircraft re-dispatched with restriction noted in flight release
l4_steps.kpi: MEL-cleared aircraft released within 30 minutes of defect; on-time departure recovery ≥ 85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa Operations and AMOS operate as separate systems; MEL deferrals must be manually mirrored to flight release, creating risk of dispatching crew without restriction awareness

l4_steps.name: Classify AOG severity and estimate RTA
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (AOG workflow module)
l4_steps.input: Confirmed AOG defect record, affected flight schedule, station capability matrix
l4_steps.output: AOG severity code (AOG-1 / AOG-2 / AOG-3), Return-to-Airworthy (RTA) estimate, passenger impact assessment
l4_steps.kpi: AOG classification completed < 10 minutes of MEL decision; RTA estimate accuracy ± 1 hour for 80% of events
l4_steps.pain_point: RTA estimates at remote outstations with limited history are often optimistic; underestimation cascades into multiple re-protection waves, amplifying passenger disruption costs

l4_steps.name: Alert station maintenance and mobilise team
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS / Airline Crew Communication Platform
l4_steps.input: AOG classification, station engineer roster, aircraft bay location
l4_steps.output: Station LAME and supporting technicians dispatched to aircraft with tooling kit
l4_steps.kpi: First engineer on aircraft within 20 minutes of AOG declaration at main bases; 45 minutes at outstations
l4_steps.pain_point: Outstations with single contracted line maintenance providers may have engineers committed to concurrent turnarounds, delaying AOG response beyond contractual SLA by 15–30 minutes

l4_steps.name: Check local parts availability for likely defect
l4_steps.input: Suspected defect ATA chapter, aircraft type, station warehouse stock snapshot
l4_steps.output: Parts availability confirmation or shortage flag sent to MCC within 10 minutes
l4_steps.kpi: Station first-time fill rate ≥ 60% for top-20 AOG consumable part numbers
l4_steps.pain_point: Inventory data in AMOS at outstations can be up to 4 hours stale if warehouse staff have not confirmed physical receipts; MCC dispatches engineers expecting parts that are not present

l4_steps.name: Perform initial inspection and fault isolation
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen FliteDeck / OEM Fault Isolation Manual (FIM)
l4_steps.input: Defect description, aircraft built-in test equipment (BITE) readout, fault codes
l4_steps.output: Confirmed ATA chapter fault code, probable cause, and required corrective action identified
l4_steps.kpi: Fault isolated within 45 minutes for 90% of LRU-level defects
l4_steps.pain_point: BITE data on older aircraft variants (e.g. A320 CFM56 legacy FDR) requires cross-referencing paper FIM charts; digital FIM integration with AMOS is not universal across fleet types

l4_steps.name: Access AMM / IPC repair procedures
l4_steps.system: Boeing Toolbox / Airbus AiRTHM / Trax (document integration)
l4_steps.input: Confirmed ATA fault code and part number from fault isolation
l4_steps.output: Approved AMM task card retrieved and printed/displayed for repair execution
l4_steps.kpi: Correct AMM revision accessible within 5 minutes; zero deferred task cards performed on superseded revisions
l4_steps.pain_point: AMM revision synchronisation between OEM publication dates and airline-approved libraries lags by 15–45 days; engineers at outstations may access a local cached version that pre-dates a critical service bulletin

l4_steps.name: Escalate to OEM engineering support if unresolved
l4_steps.system: Boeing AeroExchange / Airbus AiRTHM OEM AOG Desk portal
l4_steps.input: Unresolved fault after AMM fault isolation steps exhausted, BITE logs, photos
l4_steps.output: OEM engineering instruction (TEO/TEM) or disposition issued within agreed SLA
l4_steps.kpi: OEM first response < 2 hours (AOG priority); disposition received < 4 hours for 85% of escalations
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM AOG support SLAs differ by aircraft type and contract tier; low-utilisation carriers on basic support contracts wait up to 8 hours for dispositions, extending AOG duration into multi-day events

l4_steps.name: Activate AOG desk for emergency parts sourcing
l4_steps.system: AMOS (Purchasing / AOG Order module) + ILS Partsbase
l4_steps.input: Required part number(s), quantity, urgency (AOG priority), station and RTA
l4_steps.output: AOG purchase order raised; parts located at OEM, distributor, or pool inventory
l4_steps.kpi: AOG PO raised < 15 minutes of parts shortage confirmation; vendor acknowledgement < 1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: ILS Partsbase and AMOS purchasing are not natively integrated; coordinators toggle between platforms increasing error risk in part number / revision level transcription

l4_steps.name: Coordinate cross-fleet loan or borrow with partner airline
l4_steps.system: AMOS (Loan/Borrow module) + direct AOG desk contact
l4_steps.input: Unmet AOG PO, part number, adjacent airline AOG desk contacts at affected station
l4_steps.output: Loan agreement confirmed, part released from partner fleet, paperwork (Form 1 / 8130-3) transmitted
l4_steps.kpi: Loan agreement confirmed < 2 hours of initial AOG desk activation; traceability documents received before part installation
l4_steps.pain_point: Loan/borrow transactions require bilateral airworthiness approval (EASA Form 1 or FAA 8130-3); delays in receiving signed release documentation from partner engineers hold up installation even when part is physically available

l4_steps.name: Arrange priority shipment to AOG station
l4_steps.system: AMOS + DHL / FedEx AOG courier portal
l4_steps.input: Parts sourced and ready for dispatch, RTA, nearest airport with scheduled freight service
l4_steps.output: AOG courier shipment booked, AWB number logged in AMOS, ETA confirmed to station
l4_steps.kpi: Shipment uplift confirmed < 3 hours of part readiness; ETA accuracy ± 30 minutes for 90% of AOG shipments
l4_steps.pain_point: Same-day AOG courier capacity from remote OEM/distributor locations is limited; belly-freight dependencies on airline own schedule may add 6–12 hours versus charter courier option, but cost approval thresholds slow decision

l4_steps.name: Execute repair or LRU replacement per AMM
l4_steps.input: Serviceable part with traceability docs, approved AMM task card, tooling calibration records
l4_steps.output: Repair or replacement completed; work order in-progress record updated in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Task execution time within ± 20% of AMM estimated man-hours for 80% of LRU replacements
l4_steps.pain_point: Tooling calibration records held in a separate AMOS tooling sub-module are not always linked to the active task card; engineers must manually verify calibration status, adding 10–15 min per specialist tool

l4_steps.name: Perform functional test and duplicate inspection
l4_steps.input: Completed repair, applicable AMM functional test procedure, BITE / ground test equipment
l4_steps.output: Functional test result recorded; duplicate inspection sign-off completed in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Functional test pass rate ≥ 97% first attempt; zero releases without mandatory duplicate inspection where required by AMM
l4_steps.pain_point: At minimum-staffed outstations only one LAME may be on duty; duplicate inspection requirement cannot be fulfilled locally, forcing a flight-to-base or ferry-for-maintenance decision which adds hours to disruption

l4_steps.name: Issue Certificate of Release to Service (CRS)
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (CRS / Tech Log module)
l4_steps.input: Completed work order, functional test results, duplicate inspection sign-off, airworthiness confirmation
l4_steps.output: Signed CRS issued in AMOS; aircraft tech log updated; aircraft returned to airworthy state
l4_steps.kpi: CRS issued < 30 minutes of functional test pass; zero CRS issued against open critical defects
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS user authorisation matrix must reflect the certifying engineer's current type rating and licence scope; expired or incorrectly scoped authorisations are not always flagged at CRS sign-off, creating a regulatory compliance gap (CAR 145)

l4_steps.name: Update tech log, delay code, and disruption report
l4_steps.input: Closed work order, CRS, actual off-block time vs scheduled
l4_steps.output: IATA delay code recorded, passenger disruption cost captured, AOG event closed in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Delay code accuracy ≥ 98% (audited quarterly); disruption report filed within 2 hours of aircraft departure
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA AHM 780 delay codes for technical events require judgment calls that are inconsistently applied across MCC shifts; downstream performance analytics are therefore unreliable for root cause trending

l4_steps.name: Trigger reliability review for recurring defect
l4_steps.input: AOG event record, defect history for same ATA chapter and aircraft registration
l4_steps.output: Reliability alert raised if defect recurrence threshold exceeded; engineering investigation initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Recurring defect detection rate ≥ 95% within 3 occurrences; RCA report issued within 10 working days
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS reliability trending requires consistent ATA coding across events; MCC coding variance (see step 6.1) means recurring defects are mis-binned into different ATA sub-chapters, masking the recurrence pattern and delaying corrective action
